title_en: Resource Tax Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en:
Article 1 Units and individuals that develop taxable resources within the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under the jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China shall be taxpayers of resource tax and shall pay resource tax in accordance with the provisions of this Law.
The specific scope of taxable resources shall be determined by the Table of Resource Tax Items and Tax Rates (hereinafter referred to as the Table of Tax Items and Tax Rates) attached to this Law.

Article 2 The tax items and tax rates for resource tax shall be implemented in accordance with the Table of Tax Items and Tax Rates.
Where the Table of Tax Items and Tax Rates provides for a range tax rate, the specific applicable tax rate shall be proposed by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, taking into comprehensive consideration the grade of the taxable resource, mining conditions, and impact on the ecological environment, within the tax rate range specified in the Table of Tax Items and Tax Rates, submitted to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level for decision, and reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council for recordation. Where the Table of Tax Items and Tax Rates specifies the taxable object as raw ore or processed ore, specific applicable tax rates shall be determined separately.

Article 3 Resource tax shall be levied on an ad valorem basis or on a specific unit basis in accordance with the Table of Tax Items and Tax Rates.
Where the Table of Tax Items and Tax Rates provides that the levy may be on an ad valorem basis or on a specific unit basis at the taxpayer's option, the specific method of levy shall be proposed by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, submitted to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level for decision, and reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council for recordation.
Where resource tax is levied on an ad valorem basis, the tax payable shall be calculated by multiplying the sales amount of taxable resource products (hereinafter referred to as taxable products) by the specific applicable tax rate. Where resource tax is levied on a specific unit basis, the tax payable shall be calculated by multiplying the sales volume of taxable products by the specific applicable tax rate.
Where taxable products are mineral products, they include raw ore and processed ore products.

Article 4 Where a taxpayer mines or produces taxable products under different tax items, it shall separately account for the sales amounts or sales volumes of taxable products under different tax items; where it fails to separately account for them or cannot accurately provide the sales amounts or sales volumes of taxable products under different tax items, the higher tax rate shall apply.

Article 5 Where a taxpayer mines or produces taxable products for its own use, it shall pay resource tax in accordance with the provisions of this Law; however, where the products are used for continuous production of taxable products, no resource tax shall be paid.

Article 7 Under any of the following circumstances, the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government may decide on exemptions or reductions of resource tax:
(1) The taxpayer suffers major losses due to accidents, natural disasters, or other reasons during the mining or production of taxable products;
(2) The taxpayer mines associated minerals, low-grade ores, or tailings.
The specific measures for the exemption or reduction of resource tax as provided in the preceding paragraph shall be proposed by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, submitted to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level for decision, and reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council for recordation.

Article 8 A taxpayer shall separately account for the sales amounts or sales volumes of the items eligible for tax exemption or reduction; where it fails to separately account for them or cannot accurately provide the sales amounts or sales volumes, no tax exemption or reduction shall be granted.

Article 9 Resource tax shall be collected and administered by the tax authorities in accordance with this Law and the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection.
The tax authorities and the relevant departments such as natural resources shall establish a working coordination mechanism to strengthen the collection and administration of resource tax.

Article 10 For a taxpayer selling taxable products, the time when the obligation to pay tax arises shall be the day of receiving the sales payment or obtaining the evidence of the right to collect the sales payment; for a taxpayer using taxable products for its own use, the time when the obligation to pay tax arises shall be the day of transferring the taxable products.
Article 11 A taxpayer shall declare and pay resource tax to the tax authority at the place where the taxable products are mined or produced.

Article 12 Resource tax shall be declared and paid on a monthly or quarterly basis; where it cannot be calculated and paid on a fixed period basis, it may be declared and paid on a transaction-by-transaction basis.
Where a taxpayer declares and pays tax on a monthly or quarterly basis, it shall go through the tax declaration formalities and pay the tax to the tax authority within fifteen days from the end of the month or quarter; where it declares and pays tax on a transaction-by-transaction basis, it shall go through the tax declaration formalities and pay the tax within fifteen days from the day when the tax obligation arises.

Article 13 Where a taxpayer, tax authority, or any of their personnel violates the provisions of this Law, legal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection and the provisions of relevant laws and regulations.

Article 14 The State Council, based on the needs of national economic and social development and in accordance with the principles of this Law, shall pilot the levy of a water resource tax on units and individuals that draw surface water or groundwater. Where the water resource tax is levied, the collection of water resource fees shall cease.
The water resource tax shall apply differential tax rates based on local water resource conditions, types of water use, and economic development.
The measures for implementing the pilot water resource tax shall be prescribed by the State Council and reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for recordation.
Within five years from the coming into force of this Law, the State Council shall report to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the pilot situation of the water resource tax levy and promptly submit proposals to amend the law.

Article 15 Enterprises that cooperatively exploit onshore and offshore petroleum resources between Chinese and foreign parties shall pay resource tax according to law.
Where a contract for the cooperative exploitation of onshore or offshore petroleum resources between Chinese and foreign parties was lawfully concluded before November 1, 2011, during the validity period of such contract, the enterprises shall continue to pay mining area usage fees in accordance with the relevant state provisions and shall not pay resource tax; after the contract expires, resource tax shall be paid according to law.

Article 16 For the purposes of this Law, the following terms have the meanings ascribed to them below:
(1) Low-yield oil and gas fields include onshore low-yield oil fields, onshore low-yield gas fields, offshore low-yield oil fields, and offshore low-yield gas fields. An onshore low-yield oil field refers to an oil field where the recoverable reserves of crude oil per square kilometer are less than 250,000 cubic meters; an onshore low-yield gas field refers to a gas field where the recoverable reserves of natural gas per square kilometer are less than 250 million cubic meters; an offshore low-yield oil field refers to an oil field where the recoverable reserves of crude oil per square kilometer are less than 600,000 cubic meters; an offshore low-yield gas field refers to a gas field where the recoverable reserves of natural gas per square kilometer are less than 600 million cubic meters.
(2) High-sulfur natural gas refers to natural gas with a hydrogen sulfide content of 30 grams or more per cubic meter.
(3) Tertiary oil recovery refers to the continued extraction of oil after secondary oil recovery by means such as polymer flooding, compound flooding, foam flooding, water-alternating-gas flooding, carbon dioxide flooding, and microbial flooding.
(4) Deep-water oil and gas fields refer to oil and gas fields where the water depth exceeds 300 meters.
(5) Heavy oil refers to crude oil with a formation viscosity of 50 millipascal-seconds or greater per second or a crude oil density of 0.92 grams per cubic centimeter or greater.
(6) High pour-point oil refers to crude oil with a pour point higher than 40 degrees Celsius.
(7) A mine in decline refers to a mine with a designed mining lifespan exceeding 15 years, and where the remaining recoverable reserves have fallen below 20% of the originally designed recoverable reserves, or the remaining mining lifespan does not exceed five years. A mine in decline shall be determined on the basis of each individual mine under the mining enterprise.

Article 17 This Law shall come into force on September 1, 2020. The Interim Regulation of the People's Republic of China on Resource Tax promulgated by the State Council on December 25, 1993 shall be simultaneously abolished.
